content.content:
---
name: memsearch-index-path-drift
description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook read its path config from a Windows-era ~/Desktop/DEV path and silently fell back, indexing 4 of 10 memory paths for months after the Mac migration"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-15T04:07:30.329Z
  originSessionId: 75381393-88b6-4b65-960d-6613e08f7060
---

`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`.

**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout).

Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.

**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.

**How to apply:**
- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.

**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.

Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.

**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.

**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.

The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.

That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.

**A second signature the `Desktop/DEV` grep cannot catch:** `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (dated 2026-08-08) had been through a bad `claude` to `Codex` find-replace, so it told Codex to read `~/.Codex/global-memory/`, `~/.Codex/projects/<slug>/memory/` and `~/.Codex/Codex-memory-compiler/daily/` — none of which exist. Grep for `.Codex` (capital C) as well as `Desktop/DEV` when auditing migration damage. Also check which AGENTS.md the harness actually reads: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` was correct but referenced by nothing.

Resolved 2026-09-01: `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is now a symlink to `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, so the pair has one home and cannot drift again. `setup-agents-symlinks.sh` was also sourcing `CLAUDE.md` for that link — the one thing `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids — and now sources `AGENTS.md`. Running that script used to recreate the bug.

Repaired 2026-09-01: path corrected to `~/DEV`, required sources now push a visible "SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file" block into `additionalContext` instead of failing silently, and the hook now also injects `global-memory/USER.md` + `MEMORY.md` (replacing a prose rule in `CLAUDE.md` that nothing enforced). The KeystoneOS snapshot is pointed at, not pasted.

Related: [[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] (found while fixing that), [[secondbrain-vault-location]] (the vault move that stranded the fallback), [[backup-sync-system]]
---
name: memsearch-hook-timeout-cap
description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook's fixed 45s cap was outrun by corpus growth, so every session-end index timed out and incremental recall silently degraded to the 09:00 nightly; fixed 2026-09-02 by detaching the indexer"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-09-02T12:33:29.526Z
  originSessionId: 00fe7fc2-f53c-471d-b407-c777e8cc679c
---

`~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` (SessionEnd) ran `memsearch index <10 paths>` through
`spawnSync` with a **45s cap**, sized in July against a "~17s fixed floor, ~5s incremental"
measurement. Measured again 2026-09-02 against the current corpus (~1,450 files;
`SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings` alone is 593 and `SecondBrain/Knowledge` 334):

| run | time |
|---|---|
| no-op, nothing new to embed | **33s** (was ~17s) |
| one day of accumulated content | **278s** (232 chunks, ~1s/chunk) |

So the cap left ~12s of embedding budget — under a dozen new chunks. **Every ordinary
session-end index was timing out.** Incremental indexing had quietly degraded to "whatever
the 09:00 nightly full reindex picks up", leaving search up to 24h stale.

**Why it stayed invisible for weeks.** Three dampers stacked:
`daily-backup.ps1` resets `.memsearch-timeout-streak` every morning, the escalation
threshold is 6 consecutive timeouts, and the hook writes only to `.memsearch-index.log`
below that. So a normal day of 2-4 session-ends never reached the threshold and never
surfaced. It took **six session-ends inside 47 minutes** (2026-09-01, 21:09-21:56) to
produce a 7-long streak and one `.errors.log` line. The alarm fired on burst *frequency*,
never on the underlying constant failure.

**The misread that line invites:** ETIMEDOUT + a clustered burst pattern-matches
[[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] (session-end lock contention), and the hook's own comments
say exactly that. It was not contention — `pgrep`/`lsof` showed no holder and the DB was
healthy. **Time the actual command before believing the comment.**

**Fix (2026-09-02): detached background worker.** The hook now re-execs itself as
`node memsearch-sync.js --worker` with `detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'` and `.unref()`,
then exits — measured **42ms**. The worker keeps the entire original body, so it owns the
PID lock (clustered session-ends still elect one indexer), writes `INDEX_LOG`, and runs
every error branch. Its `spawnSync` cap is now 600s: a runaway guard, not a budget, so an
ETIMEDOUT there genuinely means ">10 minutes".

- `stdio: 'ignore'` is **not optional** — inherited or piped stdio keeps the harness's pipe
  open and it waits for the child anyway, rebuilding the timeout with extra steps.
- Self-respawn, **not** an `sh -c` wrapper: the wrapper would discard the lock ownership
  and all four error-classification branches.
- The old header justified staying synchronous with a **Windows** process-group race.
  That rationale died with the 2026-08-05 migration; the comment now says so, because the
  next reader would otherwise "restore" the bug.

**How to apply:**
- A fixed timeout sized against a measured corpus is a **dated** number. When the corpus is
  something that grows every day (the vault, meetings, dailies), the cap has an expiry date
  nobody writes down. Prefer detaching over raising a cap; if a cap must stay, record the
  measurement and the date beside it so drift is visible.
- Never size a SessionEnd hook to block. Session teardown cannot wait minutes, so any
  design where "correct" means minutes must be asynchronous.
- Both harnesses wire their own copy. `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` is now a
  **symlink** to the Claude copy (2026-09-02) so the pair cannot drift again — same fix as
  `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`. Before "fixing a hook", ask which copy the harness wires; see
  [[memsearch-index-path-drift]] for the four-copy history.
- `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1` still has a 45s
  `WaitForExit(45000)`, but nothing wires it (Codex uses `hooks.json` → the `.js`). Dead
  Windows-era code; left alone deliberately.

Related: [[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]], [[memsearch-index-path-drift]],
[[memory-compiler-pipeline]], [[backup-sync-system]], [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]

**2026-09-22 — a slow nightly index was the Mac sleeping, not memsearch.** The daily backup's
full index took 18 min for 0 new chunks (09-21 09:44) and 15 min for 309 chunks (09-21 18:12).
Timed while awake: no-op ~9s fixed startup, `dev-docs` (763 files) no-op 26s, full set 83s with
79 new chunks (~0.7s/chunk). `pmset -g log` showed 5-second DarkWakes in the morning window and
Idle Sleep twice mid-run in the evening. Fix: launchd `dailybackup` + the three data pulls now run
under `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s` (`-s` holds only on AC; lid-shut on battery still sleeps).
**How to apply:** before tuning memsearch, line the slow window up against `pmset -g log`.
Same session: `daily-backup.ps1` now resolves `{DEV}` in index paths (it had skipped
`KeystoneOS/decisions`). Jev/TypeSafe does not help indexing: it judges, it does not embed.

name: memsearch-index-is-destructive
description: "`memsearch index <paths>` deletes every indexed source outside the given paths — never run it with a partial or test path set; plus the 2026-10-07 Windows failure causes"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4f57cc78-0bf6-4202-bd61-8f428a3c6dca
  modified: 2026-10-07T22:05:05.745Z
---

`memsearch index <paths>` is **never read-only**. It reconciles the collection against
the path set it is given and deletes every indexed source not under those paths
(core.py `index()` → store.py delete). An empty or partial path set wipes the rest.

On 2026-10-07 a diagnostic run against an empty temp dir deleted ~12,900 of ~31,000
vectors before it was stopped. Recovery: a full re-index over all 13 paths in
`KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json`, which takes hours on Windows (~3 s/chunk).
`memsearch stats` counts tombstones until compaction, so use `count(*)` for live rows.

**Why:** a "just timing it" run silently destroyed 40% of the index.
**How to apply:** never pass a test or partial path set to `memsearch index`. To time
indexing, use a throwaway collection or time `memsearch search`. For a catch-up run,
use `~/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1`: it resolves the full path set and holds
the hook's lock.

Windows failure causes found the same day:
- **10-06 "Milvus unreachable":** Docker Desktop's vpnkit port forward to
  milvus-standalone flapped after days of uptime through Modern Standby. Milvus itself
  never restarted. A Docker restart cleared it.
- **10-07 ETIMEDOUT ×9:** low free RAM (1–2 GB) slowed indexing to ~1.2 s/chunk, so the
  hook's 600s cap killed every run partway. The cap was raised to 3h on 2026-10-07.
  The streak never resets on Windows because no nightly reindex runs there.

Related: [[memsearch-hook-timeout-cap]], [[automation-cadence]].

## 7. Other infrastructure: keep / simplify / retire (ranked by evidence × payoff)

| # | Component | Call | Evidence | Risk of acting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Docker Desktop + Milvus + MinIO + etcd | **Retire (Windows)** | §3, §4, §5 | Low with the 30-day volume hold; rollback is one compose command |
| 2 | `memory-index-paths.json` vault paths + silent skip | **Fix now** | 3/12 roots MISSING; Zatsiorsky 8 vs 53; hook has no log line for skipped roots [M] | None — pure gain; do it before any backend work |
| 3 | compiler per-session SDK flush | **Simplify** | 608 flush sessions/30 d; 102 "session limit" failures on 09-27 alone; 66 transcript-missing skips [M]. Options: batch to one flush per day (or per `/closeout`), back off on rate-limit, use the cheapest model for the flush (check which model `flush.py` requests — not measured) | Medium: same-day "Recent Daily Log" freshness drops from per-sessio
| 4 | dev-docs in the memory index | **Simplify** | 802 files / 2.0M tokens = 68% of the index; polluted 5/10 real-query results with QUEUE/STATUS files [M] | Keep them indexed but as a separate FTS table/collection with a `--scope` flag; default `mem search` to memory + vault |
| 5 | context-mode (FTS5 plugin) | **Keep** | 448 `ctx_search`/30 d; 70 MB content DB; strongest keyword ranker on the machine [M] | It overlaps memsearch's role; after §5 it and `mem` are the two keyword paths (interactive vs scripted). Acceptable; document the split |
| 6 | `skill-router` UserPromptSubmit hook | **Evaluate, likely retire** | 21 KB Python + 220 KB roster, 5 s cap, 1 timeout/30 d; sample recall prompt routed to `ctx-search` instead of `memory-write` [M]. Claude 5 selects from skill descriptions unaided | Unknown benefit — run 2 weeks logging its suggestion vs the skill actually invoked (both are in transcripts), then decide. [I] that it is a pre-
| 7 | Hard char caps (USER 1,375 / MEMORY 2,500; compiler 20k) | **Keep as editorial discipline, relabel** | Startup injection is 6k tokens = 0.6% of 1M [M]; the compiler's 20k cap truncated a 47k `index.md` and was already replaced by a pointer [M] | Raising caps costs nothing now; the value of the caps was curation, not budget. Say so in `memory-write` so nobody "optimises" them away |
| 8 | Duplicated Tier A slugs (Mac + Windows copies of the same notes) | **Keep, dedupe in the index** | Both slug families exist on both machines; memsearch hits resolve to the Mac copy [M] | Index one family per note (prefer the current machine's) to avoid double hits |
| 9 | Hook hygiene | **Fix** | Dead unguarded Mac-path `dcg` entry runs per Bash call; `.errors.log` truncated rather than rotated (no 30-day ledger possible today); `ms-search` referenced by `memory-write` but absent on Windows; Codex `memsearch-sync.ps1` 45 s/no cooldown still wired [M] | Trivial edits; the two-copies trap applies (`~/.codex/skills` mirrors 13 SKILL.md files) |
| 10 | graphify (6 `graphify-out` dirs) | **Not assessed** | Usage not measured; different job (structure/relations), no overlap with recall | — |
| 11 | permission-gate shadow hook | **Not assessed** | Shadow-mode logger only (`shadow.jsonl`); 1.7 KB | — |
| 12 | Scheduled tasks | **Prune with #1** | `memsearch-drain-once` still Ready after finishing; `-weekly` becomes moot | — |

### 7.1 Overlap: what each recall-related layer uniquely does

| Layer | Corpus | Retrieval type | Callable from | Unique job |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| memsearch + Milvus | 12 configured roots (9 reachable here), 18,360 chunks | dense (bge-m3) + keyword hybrid, chunk-level | shell → Claude Bash, Codex hooks, PowerShell scripts | Only layer with semantic matching; only one that indexes transcripts/dailies/dev-docs/codex memories together |
| context-mode (FTS5 plugin) | Whatever was captured or `ctx_index`ed: session outputs, tool results, auto-memory events (70 MB content DB) | BM25 + trigram + RRF + proximity rerank | Claude via MCP only (as tested) | Keeps large tool outputs out of context; session-timeline recall of decisions/errors. Does **not** index the memory roots unless told to |
| graphify (6 `graphify-out` dirs) | Per-repo code/docs | graph query (communities, paths, god nodes) | Claude via skill | Structure and relationships within a project; not fact recall |
| claude-memory-compiler | Writes `daily/` and `knowledge/` from transcripts; injects a pointer at start | none — it is a **writer**, not a retriever | hooks (SessionEnd/PreCompact/SessionStart) | Produces the curated daily log and 180 articles that the retrievers then search |
| Tier A memory + `MEMORY.md` index + global USER/MEMORY | ~58 notes per machine slug, 1-line index each | auto-injected (Tier 0), then Read by name | harness | Zero-cost recall for anything with a line in the index; the layer the pilot mostly exercised |
| rg / Grep over the same directories | any file on disk | exact/regex, file-level | everywhere | What the model reaches for 10× more often than memsearch [M]; no index to drift |

The overlap is between the first two and rg: three keyword-capable retrievers over
partly-overlapping corpora, plus one dense retriever whose unique contribution the pilot
could not distinguish from BM25 at n=10. graphify and the compiler do not overlap with them.

def _persist_compilation(response: str, log_path: Path) -> int:
    """Write articles, index rows, and the log entry from the agent's output.

    Returns the number of article files written.
    """
    written = 0
    for m in _ARTICLE_RE.finditer(response):
        dest = _safe_article_path(m.group("path"))
        body = m.group("body").strip()
        if dest is None or not body:
            print(f"  Skipped invalid article block: {m.group('path')!r}")
            continue
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(body + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        written += 1

    im = _INDEX_RE.search(response)
    if im:
        rows = [r.rstrip() for r in im.group("body").splitlines() if r.strip().startswith("|")]
        if rows:
            index_path = KNOWLEDGE_DIR / "index.md"
            if not index_path.exists() or not index_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip():
                index_path.write_text(
                    "# Knowledge Base Index\n\n"
                    "| Article | Summary | Compiled From | Updated |\n"
                    "|---------|---------|---------------|---------|\n",
                    encoding="utf-8",
                )
            with open(index_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("\n".join(rows) + "\n")
            # Rows were appended blindly, so every article UPDATE left another
            # row behind forever - 139 rows for 116 articles, one article listed
            # five times. The index is inlined into every compile prompt, so
            # that leak is paid on every run. Keep the newest row per article.
            _dedupe_index(index_path)

    lm = _LOG_RE.search(response)
    if lm and lm.group("body").strip():
        log_md = KNOWLEDGE_DIR / "log.md"
        if not log_md.exists() or not log_md.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip():
            log_md.write_text("# Build Log\n\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with open(log_md, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("\n" + lm.group("body").strip() + "\n")

    return written


def _safe_article_path(rel: str):
    """Resolve a returned article path under knowledge/{concepts,connections,qa}.

    Returns a Path, or None if the path is malformed or escapes the allowed dirs.
    """
    rel = (rel or "").strip().lstrip("/").replace("\\", "/")
    if not rel.endswith(".md"):
        return None
    parts = rel.split("/")
    if len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] not in _ALLOWED_SUBDIRS or ".." in parts:
        return None
    return KNOWLEDGE_DIR / parts[0] / parts[1]

input.summary: The memory pipeline is working: flushes and compiles succeeded today, memsearch answers queries (48,221 chunks), the nightly 13-path index ran OK at 06:53, and the global-memory caps hold. Nothing is critical. The problems are drift and silent failures. The compile lock can let two compiles run at once (it happened on 10-16), the knowledge index lists 7 articles that do not exist, the weekly adjudicate run failed on 10-18 without raising an alert, and every flush after 18:00 recompiles the whole day's log. Tier A memory has a Windows contradiction and a false claim that memsearch skips the Windows-slug folders: it indexes a stale copy of them and returns it in search results.

findings.title: Compile lock lets a second compile reclaim a live lock in the same second; two compiles ran at once on 10-16
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/compile.log lines 610-644: at 2026-10-16 23:00:07 two auto compiles started (pid 1883 and 1884). Both listed the same files (2026-10-14.md and 2026-10-16.md), their output interleaved, both wrote articles, and they reported $2.37 and $2.40 (KB went from 490 to 496). Code path: guardrails.py:132 acquire_lock opens the file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, then writes the JSON payload in a separate step (133-134). read_lock (104-111) returns None on JSONDecodeError, which includes an empty file. acquire_lock:140-143 treats None as 'unreadable lock, treat as stale', unlinks the file and retries. A process that arrives inside the create-to-write gap therefore deletes the live lock and takes it. The code allows this, and the log shows it fired once; the race was not reproduced.
findings.impact: The same log gets compiled twice in parallel, roughly doubling spend for that run. Both processes write state.json, index.md and the article files concurrently, so the last writer wins. Article updates or ingested entries can be lost or duplicated without any error.
findings.fix: Write the payload atomically: write a temp file, then os.link or os.rename it into place under O_EXCL semantics. Or treat an empty or unparseable lock younger than a few seconds (by file mtime) as held, not stale. Only reclaim a lock with no payload when its mtime is older than STALE_LOCK_SECONDS. Add a test that runs two acquire_lock calls with the write step delayed.

File with no row: concepts/concurrent-session-merge-state-check.md. log.md lines 483, 693 and 743 say these articles were 'created'. After excluding valid daily/ links there are 18 unique broken targets (62 refs). The two missing connections are the most-linked broken targets in the KB, with 20 and 7 inbound refs. compile.py _persist_compilation (124-170) appends INDEX and LOG rows from the model response whether or not a matching ARTICLE block was written, so a response that lists an article in its index block without emitting the body leaves a phantom row. session-start.py:84 reports the row count as the article count ('522 compiled articles') next to a disk breakdown that sums to 516, and never flags the gap.

findings.title: Closeout empties .errors.log without archiving, so alerts written between commits disappear
findings.evidence: The newest archive is transcripts/.errors.log.archive-2026-10-11. global-memory commit fe1fe4b (closeout 2026-10-22 08:33) deletes 2 lines from .errors.log (a daily-backup 5-error line and compiler-backlog) and adds no archive file. ~/.claude/skills/backup/SKILL.md:43 and claude-stack-doctor/SKILL.md:89 say to archive before clearing; closeout/SKILL.md:46 only says the file 'must be empty'. flush.log:2847 records FLUSH_ERROR at 2026-10-21 20:16, and flush.py:380-383 escalates that to .errors.log. compile.log:715 shows a batch-cap escalation the same minute. .errors.log was empty at commit c93d860 (10-20 closeout). The 10-22 06:05 commit e1f674f has no 2026-10-21 lines, and `git log -S '2026-10-21T'` on the file returns nothing. Those alerts are not in any commit or archive.
findings.impact: Session-start alerts, such as a failed memory flush, can be wiped before Eric sees them, and no history is left to show the pattern.
findings.fix: Have closeout use the same archive-then-clear step as backup and stack-doctor (one appended ledger file, e.g. .errors-ledger.log, rather than dated copies). Or make the SessionStart hook copy each line it surfaces into a ledger.
findings.known_where: ~/.claude/audits/2026-09-30-memory-infra-audit.md §7 row 9 ('.errors.log truncated rather than rotated'). That audit did not record the loss of specific alerts.

findings.title: Every flush after 18:00 recompiles the whole day's log (~$1 per run); 17 of 128 logs have been compiled 2 to 5 times
findings.evidence: flush.py maybe_trigger_compilation (214-254): after COMPILE_AFTER_HOUR it compiles today's log whenever the log's hash differs from state.json. Every flush appends to today's log, so the hash always differs. compile.log: 2026-10-22.md was compiled at 18:12 and again at 20:03 ($1.11 and $0.99, each with ~105k cache-creation tokens). `grep -o 'Compiling ...' | uniq -c` shows 2026-09-01 compiled 5 times; 10-10 and 10-16 4 times each; 08-06, 08-15, 09-07, 10-17 and 10-18 3 times each. state.json total_cost 128.41; per-log cost_usd sum 109.6. compile.log:504 shows a compile that failed with 'You've hit your session limit'.
findings.impact: Uses subscription quota on repeat work (the session limit has been hit). Each recompile also rewrites the same articles, which risks churn and near-duplicates.
findings.fix: Compile today's log once, at a set time (e.g. the first flush after 22:00, or a launchd job at 23:30 under caffeinate). Or compile only the diff: store the byte offset already compiled and pass only the new sections.

findings.title: The weekly adjudicate and memlint run on 10-18 failed its LLM steps, exited 0 and raised no alert; the job is not under caffeinate
findings.evidence: scripts/adjudicate.log:390-429: the run started 2026-10-18 04:33 (plist StartCalendarInterval is Sunday 02:30). findings.title: The compiler-backlog alert's count is stale; the real backlog is 1 failed log (2026-10-16.md)
findings.evidence: transcripts/.errors.log (1 line, 18:11 local) reads '2 log(s) backlogged'. compile.log:754 shows the 20:01 run said 'Batch cap: 1 log(s) backlogged', but guardrails.escalate (76-92) skips writing when the last line already contains the marker. findings.title: flush.py deletes the session context file even when the flush fails
findings.evidence: flush.py:380-392: on FLUSH_ERROR it logs the error, appends the error text to the daily log and escalates, then runs context_file.unlink(missing_ok=True) unconditionally at line 392. flush.log:2800-2849: the flush of session b5e553b3 at 18:22:59 on 10-21 failed at 20:16:19 ('Can't reach the API server ... ENOTFOUND'). The same session's earlier flush at 16:50 succeeded, so only the content after 16:50 was lost. compiler docs/STATUS.md Gotchas lists deletion on success and on duplicate-skip, but not on error.
findings.impact: Context from a session whose flush fails (network loss or sleep) is not captured into memory and cannot be retried.
findings.fix: On FLUSH_ERROR, move the context file to scripts/_stranded-archive/ instead of deleting it, and have the next successful flush or a manual step retry it.

findings.title: Compile lock lets a second compile reclaim a live lock in the same second; two compiles ran at once on 10-16
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/compile.log lines 610-644: at 2026-10-16 23:00:07 two auto compiles started (pid 1883 and 1884). Both listed the same files (2026-10-14.md and 2026-10-16.md), their output interleaved, both wrote articles, and they reported $2.37 and $2.40 (KB went from 490 to 496). Code path: guardrails.py:132 acquire_lock opens the file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, then writes the JSON payload in a separate step (133-134). read_lock (104-111) returns None on JSONDecodeError, which includes an empty file. acquire_lock:140-143 treats None as 'unreadable lock, treat as stale', unlinks the file and retries. A process that arrives inside the create-to-write gap therefore deletes the live lock and takes it. The code allows this, and the log shows it fired once; the race was not reproduced.
findings.impact: The same log gets compiled twice in parallel, roughly doubling spend for that run. Both processes write state.json, index.md and the article files concurrently, so the last writer wins. Article updates or ingested entries can be lost or duplicated without any error.
findings.fix: Write the payload atomically: write a temp file, then os.link or os.rename it into place under O_EXCL semantics. Or treat an empty or unparseable lock younger than a few seconds (by file mtime) as held, not stale. Only reclaim a lock with no payload when its mtime is older than STALE_LOCK_SECONDS. Add a test that runs two acquire_lock calls with the write step delayed.

findings.title: Compile lock lets a second compile reclaim a live lock in the same second; two compiles ran at once on 10-16
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/compile.log lines 610-644: at 2026-10-16 23:00:07 two auto compiles started (pid 1883 and 1884). Both listed the same files (2026-10-14.md and 2026-10-16.md), their output interleaved, both wrote articles, and they reported $2.37 and $2.40 (KB went from 490 to 496). Code path: guardrails.py:132 acquire_lock opens the file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, then writes the JSON payload in a separate step (133-134). read_lock (104-111) returns None on JSONDecodeError, which includes an empty file. acquire_lock:140-143 treats None as 'unreadable lock, treat as stale', unlinks the file and retries. A process that arrives inside the create-to-write gap therefore deletes the live lock and takes it. The code allows this, and the log shows it fired once; the race was not reproduced.
findings.impact: The same log gets compiled twice in parallel, roughly doubling spend for that run. Both processes write state.json, index.md and the article files concurrently, so the last writer wins. Article updates or ingested entries can be lost or duplicated without any error.
findings.fix: Write the payload atomically: write a temp file, then os.link or os.rename it into place under O_EXCL semantics. Or treat an empty or unparseable lock younger than a few seconds (by file mtime) as held, not stale. Only reclaim a lock with no payload when its mtime is older than STALE_LOCK_SECONDS. Add a test that runs two acquire_lock calls with the write step delayed.

findings.title: Auto-captured daily logs and the compiled KB hold athlete health/RTP content with no redaction step, and all of it is indexed into memsearch
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/index.md row 10 (line ~14) indexes an article about return-to-competition CMJ reports for an athlete named in the row, including 'Post-Op Low' terminology. `grep -rli 'post-op|ACL|concussion|injur|return-to-competition|RTP' knowledge daily` matches 88 files; `grep -rli 'dexa|body comp'` matches 34 (many may be project mentions only; not inspected). `grep -n 'redact|health|PII|athlete' scripts/flush.py` returns nothing. knowledge/ and daily/ are gitignored (.gitignore), but both are in memory-index-paths.json and so stored in ~/.memsearch/milvus.db.
findings.impact: Identifiable athlete health information can build up in stores that are automatically captured, indexed and backed up. This conflicts with the DexaProject / Jev health-data handling rules. Only one identifiable case was confirmed.
findings.fix: Add a rule to the flush prompt ('do not record athlete names with medical, injury or body-composition details; refer to them by role') and a regex guard in flush.py. Have Eric review the one confirmed article and decide whether to scrub it. Confirm whether these stores reach any cloud copy.

findings.title: The compiler-backlog alert's count is stale; the real backlog is 1 failed log (2026-10-16.md)
findings.evidence: transcripts/.errors.log (1 line, 18:11 local) reads '2 log(s) backlogged'. compile.log:754 shows the 20:01 run said 'Batch cap: 1 log(s) backlogged', but guardrails.escalate (76-92) skips writing when the last line already contains the marker. Recomputing from state.json against file hashes: 128 logs, 0 unseen, 0 changed, 1 not succeeded: 2026-10-16.md status=failed attempts=1 ('API Error: Can't reach the API server ... ENOTFOUND'). It is not quarantined and will be retried. The last successful compile was 2026-10-22T20:03:40 (2026-10-22.md). Because the batch takes the newest 2 logs and today's log is always one of them after 18:00, the backlog drains only 1 older log per run.
findings.impact: The session-start alert overstates the backlog and stays until it is cleared by hand. Minor.
findings.fix: Have escalate() replace the last line when the marker matches, instead of skipping. To clear the backlog now, run once by hand: `uv run --directory ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler python scripts/compile.py --file 2026-10-16.md`.

findings.title: flush.py deletes the session context file even when the flush fails
findings.evidence: flush.py:380-392: on FLUSH_ERROR it logs the error, appends the error text to the daily log and escalates, then runs context_file.unlink(missing_ok=True) unconditionally at line 392. flush.log:2800-2849: the flush of session b5e553b3 at 18:22:59 on 10-21 failed at 20:16:19 ('Can't reach the API server ... ENOTFOUND'). The same session's earlier flush at 16:50 succeeded, so only the content after 16:50 was lost. compiler docs/STATUS.md Gotchas lists deletion on success and on duplicate-skip, but not on error.
findings.impact: Context from a session whose flush fails (network loss or sleep) is not captured into memory and cannot be retried.
findings.fix: On FLUSH_ERROR, move the context file to scripts/_stranded-archive/ instead of deleting it, and have the next successful flush or a manual step retry it.
